newsitem.title: EGYPT: Saudi prince sets up Egypt land reclamation firm.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince sets up Egypt land reclamation firm.

text.p: Saudi Arabian investor Prince al-Waleed bin Talal has received approval for a land reclamation and agricultural project in a remote southern Egyptian valley, his third major investment in the country.

The president of Egypt's General Authority for Investment, Ibrahim Fawzy, told Reuters on Thursday the prince was setting up the Kingdom Agricultural Company in Toshka as part of the South Valley Development Project.
The Egyptian government is seeking investors for its ambitious scheme to transform uninhabited desert close to the Sudanese border into an area as rich as the Nile Delta.

"He (Prince Talal) has simply established a company to operate in Toshka," Fawzy told Reuters. "Its issued capital is 100 million pounds and authorised capital is one billion pounds ($295 million). It will operate in land reclamation."
The allocation to the prince of almost 450,000 acres (180,000 hectares) for the project makes him the largest agricultural land owner in Egyptian history, his office said in a statement in July.

The project is the billionaire prince's latest in the Middle East. In July the Palestinian firm PADICO said he invested $10 million in the flagship firm, the first foray by a prominent Saudi investor in the nascent Palestinian market.
The prince this year also added Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest to his huge international portfolio of investments and is eyeing other opportunities in the country as it reconstructs.
Prince al-Waleed's newest project in Egypt is the first in the South Valley to be authorised under Egypt's new incentives law which came into force this month, Fawzy said.
The law, which grants a 20-year tax holiday, reflects Egypt's aim to develop priority sectors by luring investors by cutting red tape and offering incentives.

New projects are no longer subject to a lengthy approval process. Instead, investors notify Egyptian authorities of their project and receive incentives if they are in one of 16 priority sectors. Egypt is aggressively trying to attract investors to the South Valley, President Hosni Mubarak's pet project.
"We will have more applications for Toshka but we do not keep anything in the pipeline. We just grab it and establish it immediately," Fawzy said.
He said Saudis are the biggest Arab investors in Egypt, with interests worth 3.4 billion pounds ($1 billion) in 383 projects.

The prince's office has said he would initially hold a 60 percent stake in the company, while his Kingdom Holding Co and Kingdom Cayman Co would own 20 percent each. Stakes would be available to Arab and foreign investors later.

The project is the prince's first agricultural venture and one of several investments in Egypt this year. He is building a Four Seasons hotel in Cairo and another in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.
The prince, a nephew of Saudi King Fahd, has billions of dollars in investments including hotels, theme parks and banks.
